union.summary: Fix is scoped far wider than the issue: single-dash setext headings (`Heading\n-`) are silently killed everywhere in the notes preview
union.evidence: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` in the forked `lheadingRule` rejects a lone `-` underline unconditionally — at any nesting level, including a plain top-level paragraph with no list anywhere in sight. The originating issue is narrowly about "a list item followed by an empty nested list item"; its expected behavior only concerns the parent `<li>`. After this change, existing note content such as `Title\n-` (a perfectly ordinary CommonMark H2, the single-dash form of `Title\n---`) stops being a heading and instead renders as a paragraph followed by an empty bullet list. Nothing in the issue asks for that. A guard restricted to the in-list case (e.g. only when `state.blkIndent > 0` / the paragraph is inside a list item) would satisfy the issue with no collateral. The docs added in this PR acknowledge only that "Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched" (docs/design/notes/notes.md), i.e. they concede single-dash setext is broken, but the issue never requested that trade. Note also the PR's own plan (docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md, "Steps") lists a `top-level lone dash` test case that does not appear among the added tests, so the widest behavior change of the PR is the one left unpinned.

union.summary: ~85 lines of markdown-it's upstream `lheading` rule (plus its `asciiTrim` helper) are forked into the repo instead of being wrapped/delegated as the `list` rule is in the same file
union.evidence: `const lheadingRule: BlockRule = ...` is, by its own comment, a copy of "markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`" "with a single added guard". `ASCII_TRIM_RE`/`asciiTrim` (lines 18-23) likewise re-create markdown-it's private helper. This duplicates dependency-owned logic in a repo whose stated norm is reuse: any markdown-it upgrade that touches lheading (lazy-continuation handling, terminator scanning, token map fields) silently diverges here with nothing to detect the drift. The same file demonstrates the non-forking alternative 110 lines later — `wrappedList` captures the original `list` rule and delegates for every case but the one it cares about — so the two rules in one plugin use two different, inconsistent approaches. A pre-check-then-delegate wrapper for `lheading` (decline only when the underline candidate is a lone dash, otherwise call the stock rule) would avoid carrying the fork.

union.summary: The paragraph-interrupt relaxation covers `*` and `+` and top-level paragraphs, which is broader than the reported case
union.evidence: `wrappedList` returns true for any `isEmptyBulletLine`, and `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (lines 38-41) with no requirement that the paragraph be inside a list item. So `foo\n*` or `foo\n+` — previously plain paragraph text per CommonMark — now terminate the paragraph and emit an empty `<ul>`. The issue only describes an indented empty bullet under a parent list item; the `*`/`+` and top-level relaxations are unrequested behavior changes and are not covered by the acceptance criteria the PR's own todo doc lists.

union.summary: `getRuleFn` reaches into markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry to recover a rule function
union.evidence: `const ruler = md.block.ruler as unknown as { __rules__: Array<{...}> }` deliberately casts through an undocumented internal. The comment concedes "markdown-it's Ruler exposes no public getter". This couples the notes preview to a dependency's private shape with only a runtime `throw` as protection; the public-API alternative (`md.block.ruler.before('list', ...)` / a `paragraph`-alt rule inserted ahead of `list`, which needs no handle on the original) is not considered. Layering/abstraction concern rather than a logic defect.
